'''Helen Diana Burgess''' (28 July 1951 – 24 August 1999), was a Canadian [[Conservator-restorer|conservation]] scientist. Burgess spent her career at the [[Canadian Conservation Institute]] ("CCI"), where she was a Senior Conservation Scientist.<ref name=Queens>{{cite web | last = Gulcev	| first = Makedonka | title = Helen Burgess, (MAC 1979, research), Senior Conservation Scientist, Canadian Conservation Institute | publisher = Queen's University Department of Art History and Conservation | date = 2015 | url = http://www.queensu.ca/art/sites/webpublish.queensu.ca.artwww/files/files/Helen%20Burgess.pdf | access-date = 2018-05-09 }}</ref> She was a researcher in paper and textiles conservation processes and an expert in the areas of cellulose degradation analysis, conservation bleaching, washing, enzyme applications on paper, as well as aqueous and mass deacidification of paper.<ref name = Queens/><ref name = "CCI News">{{cite journal |last1= McCawley |first1= Cliff |last2= Tse |first2= Season |date= March 1998|title= Turning a page: Helen Burgess retires = Helen D. Burgess tournes la page |journal= CCI Newsletter |issue= 21|pages= 17–18}}</ref><ref name= Petherbridge>{{Cite book|title= Conservation of Library and Archive Materials and the Graphic Arts |last= Petherbridge |first= Guy |publisher=[[LexisNexis|Butterworths]]|year=1987|isbn=0-408-01466-0 |location=London|pages=328}}</ref>

==Career==

Helen Burgess obtained her Bachelor of Science (Chemistry) (Honours) from the [[University of Lethbridge]] in 1973. Burgess subsequently went to the [[University of British Columbia]], where she graduated with a Masters of Science in bio-[[organic chemistry]]. She then went on to obtain a Masters of Conservation from [[Queen's University at Kingston|Queen's University]], specializing in conservation science.<ref name = Queens/> At Queen's, her Masters [[thesis]] dealt with the degradation of cellulose during conservation bleaching treatments.<ref name= Petherbridge />

In 1978, Burgess joined CCI in its Conservation Processes Research department.<ref name = Queens/> Burgess ultimately became its Senior Conservation Scientist, a position she held until her retirement in 1998. Her primary focus was the conservation of paper artifacts,<ref name= Petherbridge /> but she also handled other materials, such as textiles. For several decades, the primary guidance for conservation bleaching practices was dominated by guidelines Burgess helped develop.<ref name = Brückle>{{cite journal |last= Brückle |first= Irene |date= December 2009 |title= Bleaching Paper in Conservation: Decision-Making Parameters |journal= Restaurator: International Journal for the Preservation of Library and Archival Material |volume= 30 |issue= 4|pages= 321–332 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url= http://cool.conservation-us.org/coolaic/sg/bpg/pcc/1987_frontmatter.pdf |title= Paper Conservation Catalogue |last= Burgess |first= Helen |date= 1987 |website= Conservation Online |publisher= Foundation of the American Institute for Conservation of Historic and Artistic Works |access-date=3 March 2017 }}</ref> Burgess was the first conservation-restoration scientist to classify the chemical analysis of treated specimens, and to find an application for bleaching agents in paper conservation.<ref name= Brückle /><ref>{{Cite web|url= https://www.cac-accr.ca/files/pdf/EJournalVol13_abstract3.pdf |title= Practical Considerations for Conservation Bleaching. Journal of the IIC-Canadian Group 13 (1988):11 – 26. |last= Burgess |first= Helen |date= 1988 |website= Journal of CAC - Archived Issues |publisher= The Canadian Association for Conservation of Cultural Property |access-date=3 March 2017 }}</ref> Burgess published numerous articles in a variety of academic journals and industry publications.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://worldcat.org/identities/lccn-nr98011644/|title=Burgess, Helen Diana 1951- |website= WorldCat Identities |publisher= OCLC Online Computer Library Center, Inc. |access-date=3 March 2017 }}</ref> Burgess was also a frequent presenter at conservation, restoration, and scientific conferences. She was one of the scientists featured on a 1990 episode of ''[[The Nature of Things]]'', "Turning to Dust", about the deterioration of paper in old books around the world and efforts to preserve them.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://curio.ca/en/video/turning-to-dust-5578/|title=''The Nature of Things''- |website= Curio.ca |publisher= CBC/Radio-Canada |access-date=25 October 2020 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://app.pch.gc.ca/application/bibicc-ccilib/detailler-detail.app?rID=ccicat1185&lang=en&ssm=true&query=&title=&authedit=&sub=&pub=&doctype=&pID=1&ps=25&sort=0&f0=&f1=Documentation+de+biblioth%C3%A8que+-+Conservation+et+restauration&f2=&f3=&f4=/|title=Catalogue record "The nature of things: Turning to dust" |website= CCI Library Catalogue and Staff Bibliography |publisher= Government of Canada |access-date=25 October 2020 }}</ref>

Burgess died a year after her retirement, in 1999.<ref name = Queens/><ref name="CCI News" /> At the annual conference of the [[Western Association for Art Conservation]] following her death, several of the presentations were dedicated to her memory.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://cool.conservation-us.org/waac/wn/wn22/wn22-1/wn22-108.html|title=Conference Review (WAAC Newsletter Jan 2000 Volume 22 Number 2)|date= January 2000 |website= Western Association for Art Conservation  |access-date=28 February 2017 }}</ref>
